Commentary.Commentary: Right then, that is it from this game. We have a few more warm-up games lined up before the main event. The ICC Women's World Cup kicks off on Tuesday, 30 September, with a thrilling opener between India Women versus Sri Lanka Women. The game will begin at 9.30 am GMT. Do join us for the early build-up and all the action as the tournament gets underway. Cheers!

Sri Lanka Women won the toss and opted to bat first, setting the stage for what looked to be a thrilling match. Despite losing an early wicket, Hasini Perera quickly took charge, relieving the pressure with a couple of impressive boundaries. Harshitha Samarawickrama was finding her rhythm at the crease while Fatima Sana from Pakistan Women managed to claim a crucial wicket, and Diana Baig was looking particularly menacing with the ball. On 7.3, when the score was 33 for 1, that's when the inevitable happened. Around 11:30 am GMT, the drizzle began to ease, and hope filled the air as the groundsmen started removing the covers. But just as it looked like we might resume play, the rain returned with a vengeance, leaving us with nothing but what-ifs.

Update - 1.56 pm GMT - We’ve just received the official update, and unfortunately, THE MATCH HAS BEEN ABANDONED! This isn’t the result we were hoping for, but it seems the rain gods have other plans today. Still, we did witness some exciting moments of cricket before the weather turned.

However, in another warm-up match, India Women are going head-to-head with England Women in Bengaluru. After electing to bowl first, India Women made an impressive impact by claiming the first wicket in just the second over of the inning to set the tone. While Amy Jones and Heather Knight put together a commendable innings, the momentum dramatically shifted in favour of the Three Lions as Nat Sciver-Brunt and Emma Lamb formed a formidable partnership. At one point, England Women were sitting at 104 for 3 in the 21st over, but now they are edging to cross the 300-run mark. Nat has brilliantly reached his century and is now eyeing 150, while Lamb has also notched up her half-century. You can switch tabs to follow the live updates while waiting for further updates in this game.
Update - 12.31 pm GMT - Nothing new to inform! The drizzle persists, and the covers are firmly placed. We're all left in suspense as the waiting game continues.
Update 11.35 am GMT - Scratch the previous update. The drizzle is back, and so are the covers. Ugh, this is frustrating!

Update 11.30 am GMT - Good news! The drizzle has eased, and the ground staff have begun removing the covers, bringing us one step closer to getting the game underway. Let's hope the pitch is ready for play soon!

Update 11.15 am GMT - We've been delayed for nearly an hour now, and we're currently awaiting updates from the ground. We'll keep you posted as soon as we receive any news. Fingers crossed the rain clears up soon and the cricketing action resumes...

Football fans? Anyone? Ousmane Dembele has been crowned the 2025 Men's Ballon d'Or winner, edging out Lamine Yamal, after leading PSG to a remarkable European treble. Meanwhile, Aitana Bonmatí has made history by claiming a record third Women's Ballon d'Or award. PSG's impressive performance also earned them the 'Club of the Year' title.

Also, the Asia Cup 2025 is heating up! India has sealed its spot in the final with a convincing win over Bangladesh yesterday, while Sri Lanka has been eliminated. The real battle now is between Pakistan and Bangladesh, both of whom suffered losses to India but won against Sri Lanka. Today's game between Pakistan and Bangladesh is crucial, as the winner will join India in the finals! The match begins at 2.30 pm GMT – don't miss the action!

Meanwhile, in a separate warm-up match, India Women are taking on England Women in Bengaluru. India Women have opted to field first and England Women are currently at 83/2 in 16 overs. Heather Knight and Nat Sciver-Brunt are at the crease, looking to build a gritty stand. You can switch tabs to follow the live updates while waiting for the rain to clear up here...

Update 10.16 am GMT - Oh no! Bad news folks, as the drizzles have started and the groundsmen have covered the pitch area with sheets. Let's keep our fingers crossed and hope it's just a passing shower. Stay tuned for more updates...

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the clash to begin! The two umpires have taken their position and the players of Pakistan Women have scattered to take their fielding positions. Fatima Sana, the skipper of Pakistan Women, will start with the new ball. Hasini Perera and Chamari Athapaththu will be the opening pair of Sri Lanka Women. Here we go...

Pakistan Women - Aliya Riaz, Eyman Fatima, Natalia Pervaiz, Sadaf Shamas, Shawaal Zulfiqar, Sidra Amin, Fatima Sana (C), Omaima Sohail, Muneeba Ali (WK), Sidra Nawaz, Diana Baig, Nashra Sandhu, Rameen Shamim, Sadia Iqbal, Syeda Aroob Shah.

Sri Lanka Women - Harshitha Samarawickrama, Hasini Perera, Imesha Dulani, Nilakshika Silva, Vishmi Gunarathne, Chamari Athapaththu (C), Dewmi Vihanga, Kavisha Dilhari, Piumi Wathsala, Anushka Sanjeewani (WK), Achini Kulasuriya, Inoka Ranaweera, Malki Madara, Sugandika Kumari, Udeshika Prabodhani.
TOSS - Sri Lanka Women have won the toss and elected to BAT first.

As the game unfolds, it will be a blend of measured accumulation and brisk acceleration. However, the warm-up match forecast looks challenging, with showers expected throughout. Let's hope it doesn't rain and we get a full game. Toss and team news in a bit...

Pakistan, meanwhile, will be eager to translate promising domestic performances into the middle with consistency. Sidra Amin has been in superb touch and topping the charts, including some centuries as well. The bowling unit led by Nashra Sandhu will test Sri Lanka’s top order, while the pace and cunning of Fatima Sana and Diana Baig could threaten in the death overs.

Sri Lanka come in with form in the head-to-head, having claimed four of the last five encounters. The left-arm spin of Inoka Ranaweera and the all-round capabilities of Chamari Athapaththu will be key, while Harshitha Samarawickrama and Vishmi Gunaratne will be keen to ride the momentum. Expect the batting line-up to fire in patches, with contributions from Hasini Perera, Nilakshi de Silva and Anushka Sanjeewani keeping the scoreboard ticking.

The stage is set at the Colombo Cricket Club Ground as Sri Lanka Women take on Pakistan Women in the third warm-up of the ICC Women’s World Cup. Chamari Athapaththu and her unit will look to seize the moment early, lifting the intensity with crisp fielding and compact batting. The crowd will be hoping for a polished display from the home side as they fine-tune for the big hunt ahead.
